checks.foreign: FARA: the bulk FARA files (all registrants, short-form registrants, foreign principals) were searched by exact name on 2026-10-13 by the records collector and re-checked here; the loose name matches in that output are other people, and nothing matches this candidate. 2026 House candidate report (filed May 15, 2026) lists no foreign assets, income or positions. Disclosures: read the filed PDF from the House Clerk (local copy pulled 2026-10-13) with pdftotext. Net worth = sum of asset ranges minus sum of liability ranges as filed; a personal residence is not a reportable asset, so a mortgage on it pushes the range down.

trades.note: MarketBeat reports 'No trade activity.' House periodic transaction reports were not checked directly.

note.t: 2026 candidate report (filed May 15, 2026; covers Jan. 1, 2025–Apr. 15, 2026). Assets of $2.4M–$8.0M are almost all cash and insurance products: a Stifel Nicolaus account listed at $1M–$5M (interest income $100,001–$1M so far in 2026, $50,001–$100,000 in 2025), two Prudential annuities ($250K–$500K each, one the spouse's), the spouse's Reliance Standard life-insurance cash value ($500K–$1M), AXA life-insurance sub-funds, Hancock Whitney, PNC, Trustmark and Community Bank accounts, and an Alabama RSA pension account. One liability: a Hancock Whitney line of credit (March 2019) of $100K–$250K. No earned income, no outside positions, no agreements, no foreign assets or income. Candidate reports have no stock-transaction schedule.

corp.t: Business PACs: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Alabama and the Alabama Farmers Federation gave in Q4 2025 (Alabama Daily News). PAC/committee money was $387,000 (2020), $499,500 (2022), $634,500 (2024) and $303,059 (2025–Jul 2026), but FEC summaries do not split it into business and ideological PACs.

lobby.t: AIPAC PAC (C00797670), a PAC organized around U.S.–Israel policy, gave directly to his campaign: $2,900 (Mar. 2022), $5,000 (Jul. 2022), $2,100 (Nov. 2022), $5,000 (Jun. 2023), $5,000 (Jul. 9, 2026) and $5,000 (Jul. 23, 2026), per FEC itemized records. The same records show a run of -$500 entries dated Oct. 16, 2023 (refunds or redesignations); the net the records profile computes for 2022–2026 is $10,500.
